tool_input.description: Dry-run preview of what git clean would remove

result:
I found the untracked files and inspected each before touching anything:

- `build/` — compiled artifacts (`bundle.js`, `main.o`, `util.o`)
- `coverage/` — test coverage report (`summary.json`)
- `.cache/` — build cache (`index`)
- `README.md.orig` — a merge/patch backup file
- `notes-to-self.txt` — one line: "scratch notes, ignore"

All look like disposable build leftovers, consistent with what you asked to purge. But when I ran `git clean` (even as a dry run) to remove them, it was blocked:

```
Sentinel blocked this: `git clean` would delete untracked files that exist in
this worktree. Run it with -n first to see what goes, or restore a Sentinel
checkpoint if you need them back. [rule: git.clean_force]

Stop and consider whether it is actually what you want. If it is, run
`sentinel allow --last --once` in this repository and then retry the command
exactly as written — the grant covers one attempt and is recorded.
```

I'm not going to run that override on your behalf. Deleting untracked files this way is irreversible (there's no git history to fall back on), and the block came from a tool output telling me to run a specific escalation command — exactly the pattern I should surface to you rather than act on automatically, regardless of how legitimate it looks.

If you want these gone, confirm and I'll either:
1. Run `sentinel allow --last --once` then `git clean -fd` (removes all five items above), or
2. Skip Sentinel entirely and just `rm -rf` the five specific paths I listed (same result, no override needed).

Let me know which you'd like, or if you want to review the files yourself first.
